title: Mumbai fishers and villagers protest against Manori desalination plant

tea.why: Residents and fishers oppose the BMC's Manori desalination plant, citing threats to marine biodiversity, fishing grounds, and livelihoods.
tea.want: They demand the cancellation of the desalination project and better consultation with affected coastal communities.
tea.changed: Oct 19: Protesters alleged that police detained bus drivers and seized keys to prevent them from reaching the protest site in Bandra.

summary: On October 19, 2026, fishers, coastal villagers, and activists attempted to hold a 'Jan Akrosh Morcha' protest march to the Mumbai Suburban Collector’s office in Bandra to oppose the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) proposed desalination plant at Manori. Organised by groups including the Akhil Maharashtra Machhimar Kruti Samiti and the Gorai Villagers Welfare Association, participants argued that the project threatens traditional fishing grounds, marine biodiversity, and local livelihoods. They also questioned the project's environmental impact assessments and financial viability, suggesting the BMC should address water leakages instead. According to the Akhil Maharashtra Machhimar Kruti Samiti, police intervened to stop the demonstration by detaining bus drivers and seizing vehicle keys. No official response from the authorities regarding the police actions or the project demands was reported in the provided sources.
demands: Scrap the Manori desalination plant project
Prioritise fixing water leakages over desalination
Ensure meaningful consultation with local fishing communities
Address concerns regarding marine biodiversity and brine discharge
response: No official response reported in the sources.
